next_steps: Start researching Plateforme agréée (PA) providers now so you can choose one that fits your invoicing volume and budget before the 2026 receiving deadline.
Check that your accounting or invoicing software can handle or export Factur-X, UBL 2.1, or CII formats, or plan to upgrade in time.
Mark 1 September 2026 (receiving invoices) and 1 September 2027 (issuing invoices) on your business calendar and revisit your readiness a few months before each date.

obligations.explanation: From 1 September 2026, your business will need to be able to receive e-invoices from suppliers in one of the accepted formats (Factur-X, UBL 2.1 or CII, all meeting the EN 16931 standard), delivered via a Plateforme agréée (PA, formerly known as PDP). Not doing so can lead to penalties of EUR 50 per invoice not issued electronically and EUR 500 per e-reporting breach, capped at EUR 15,000 per year.

This specific obligation to issue e-invoices from 1 September 2026 applies to large enterprises and ETI (mid-sized companies) using the same accepted formats and the Plateforme agréée network. Based on your profile as a small business, this particular deadline does not appear to be the one that applies to you, but it's listed here as part of the overall rollout schedule.

As an SME, your obligation to issue e-invoices (not just receive them) begins on 1 September 2027. You'll need to issue invoices in one of the accepted formats (Factur-X, UBL 2.1 or CII under EN 16931) through a Plateforme agréée. The same penalty structure applies: EUR 50 per invoice not issued electronically and EUR 500 per e-reporting breach, capped at EUR 15,000 per year.
